clue.text: Saying remove surface from fine wooden pieces

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or proverb
to dust is to wipe the film off a surface

explanation.surface: Someone advises sanding the top off some delicate bits of woodwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saying' looks like a verb introducing speech, but it is the noun SAW, an old proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawdust is the powdery residue left when timber is cut, so tiny particles of wood.

clue.text: May be completely taken in!

parts.note: reads like someone easily fooled, but means something that can dissolve wholly into a liquid

explanation.surface: A gullible person might be utterly deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that dissolves is absorbed entirely into the solvent, vanishing into it.

clue.text: Arranging to get a new vehicle

indicators.note: putting things in a new order, so the letters of the following words are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone sets about fixing up a new car for themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' rearranges the nine letters of TO GET A NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, an old kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Not all of the jauntiest people are free

indicators.note: only part of the following word is taken, so the answer sits inside it

explanation.surface: Only some of the most cheerful folk enjoy liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all of' takes the letters inside jaUNTIEst; 'people are' just joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to release from bonds, a synonym of the verb to liberate.

clue.text: Sections of the camp without aspiration

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so camp goes around the aspiration

parts.note: a camp is a collection of tents
the breathy sound of an aspirate is represented by the letter H

explanation.surface: Parts of the campsite where nobody breathes heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here means 'outside': TENTS wraps around H, the aspirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenths are equal parts into which a whole is divided, so portions or divisions.

clue.text: A play about small children making money

indicators.note: the play goes around the small children

parts.note: a drama is a play for the stage
CH is the standard abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A theatre piece featuring little kids turns out to be a money-spinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; the opening 'A' belongs to the surface and supplies no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro.

clue.text: The man who is never overruled

definitions.text: The man who is never overruled

parts.words: The man who is never overruled
parts.note: describes a ruler whose word is absolute, with nobody above to reverse his decisions

explanation.surface: A man whose decisions always stand.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat holds total power, so no one can countermand him.

clue.text: A person must be patient using such transport

definitions.text: A person must be patient using such transport

parts.words: A person must be patient using such transport
parts.note: patient here means a sick person being carried, not someone who waits calmly

explanation.surface: A traveller needs tolerance to put up with a slow service.
explanation.definitionFit: The vehicle that carries the sick or injured to hospital carries a patient by definition.

clue.text: The woman with no back-up gets the bird

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, backing up reads the word no from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A lady without support finds herself jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' reads as being booed off stage, but 'the bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: An entertainer's surprising traits —- eye-opening!

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement suggests the letters of traits are jumbled
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A performer's startling characteristics are a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' rearranges TRAITS to ARTIST, and 'eye-opening' gives E, the first letter of eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer, such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Hint leg break should elicit cheer

indicators.note: breaking the words smashes their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Suggesting someone breaks a leg should raise a smile, as theatre folk say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges the letters of HINT LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten is to brighten someone's mood, so to gladden.

clue.text: Tom has bare midriff just for show

indicators.note: Tom holds the next word within it
bare is set in the middle, like a midriff

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man flaunts his bare stomach purely for display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'midriff' put BARE in the middle of CAT. 'Tom' is a male cat, not a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is a nightclub entertainment of songs and sketches.

clue.text: Standard announcement of stupendous news

parts.note: standard is a banner or flag, and the announcement is the big type a paper uses for huge news

explanation.surface: The usual way a dramatic story is announced.
explanation.definitionFit: Front-page lines in large type across a newspaper's full width proclaim major events.

clue.text: Directions abound to gain respect

parts.note: E and S are the compass points east and south
to teem is to be plentiful

explanation.surface: Clear instructions aplenty help a person win regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard or admiration.

clue.text: No longer stress there's a supplement

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
tension is strain or stress

explanation.surface: A relief from strain comes as an added bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An extension is an addition that enlarges something, like an annexe.

clue.text: Once porn's dealt with, get food for some Americans

indicators.note: the letters are dealt out afresh, like cards, into a new order

parts.note: the possessive ending supplies no letter, leaving the word as spelt

explanation.surface: With the explicit material sorted, there's a snack for folk across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn pone is a simple cornbread eaten in the southern United States.

clue.text: The issue not available bound

parts.note: a dish that is off the menu is no longer available
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: This edition is out of stock and tied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means children, and 'bound' is a jump, not tied.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the legal sense means descendants, a person's children.

clue.text: Brown's been put inside since bent to make an example

indicators.note: brown is placed within the other letters
bending the word since twists its letters into a new order

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: A man called Brown is jailed again, crooked since, as a warning to others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' scrambles the word since, and 'put inside' signals the container; 'been' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case illustrating something.

clue.text: Caught before warming up. It's quite unfair

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
heating is warming

explanation.surface: Someone is caught before getting to grips with something, which seems unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceit to gain advantage, breaking the rules, is the very model of unfairness.

clue.text: A delightful girl many hurt with little hesitation

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
to harm is to hurt
er is a short pause in speech

explanation.surface: A lovely young woman injures lots of people with barely a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: A charmer is someone attractive and winning in manner.

clue.text: Advert about English jacket

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: to advert to something is to refer to it

explanation.surface: An advertisement promoting a British coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advert' looks like an advertisement, but is the old verb meaning refer; 'about' puts E inside REFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket, as worn by sailors.

clue.text: After this a worn-out traveller should be ready to travel on

definitions.text: After this a worn-out traveller should be ready to travel on

parts.words: After this a worn-out traveller should be ready to travel on
parts.note: the traveller is a bald tyre, not a weary person, made fit for the road again by fresh tread

explanation.surface: A tired wanderer, rested, can set off once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving an old tyre new tread lets it be used on the road again.

clue.text: Cutting a circle in wood

indicators.note: the circle is set within the wood

parts.note: a grove is a small wood
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A ring is felled in the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a long narrow cut or channel, such as one in a record.

clue.text: Pert Mexican star badly treated — constantly downtrodden

indicators.note: rough treatment scrambles the letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A cheeky Latin celebrity is mistreated and always kept down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly treated' rearranges the fifteen letters of PERT MEXICAN STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug made in the English town of Axminster lies on the floor to be walked over.

clue.text: Married — a trap for an artistic individual

parts.note: a net is used to trap animals

explanation.surface: A wedding is a snare for a creative type.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was a French painter of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: He's always prepared to take part !

definitions.text: He's always prepared to take part !

parts.words: He's always prepared to take part
parts.note: sounds like an eager volunteer, but taking a part means playing a role on stage

explanation.surface: A willing man is ready to join in anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer takes roles in plays or films.

clue.text: A worker is backed over housing

parts.note: to man something is to work it, so a man is a worker

indicators.note: the little word is is read backwards

parts.note: on can mean on top of, over

explanation.surface: A labourer is supported in taking over accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' signals the reversal of the small word; the opening 'A' belongs to the surface and adds nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large, grand house, so a dwelling.

clue.text: Preliminary plan for -striking bar

parts.note: workers on strike are out
a bar is a straight line

explanation.surface: A rough scheme for a pub during industrial action.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough sketch or summary before details are worked out.

clue.text: About to accept retiring associate's suite

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second within it

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to associate is to unite; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A partner's hotel rooms are taken back on approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' signals the reversal and 'to accept' the container; 'associate' is the verb meaning join, not a colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite can be a body of attendants, the followers of an important person.

clue.text: Angry letter to disreputable newspaper editor

parts.note: en is the name of the letter N in printing
a rag is a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone furious sends a complaint to the editor of a trashy tabloid.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is the printer's name for the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Enraged means furious, very cross.
